questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to do an exchange in a country, where I normally wouldn't go on vacation. Therefore, I chose Australia, because it was a once in a lifetime opportunity to explore a country for half a year, that is far away from Denmark. Moreover, I wanted to go to a country, where it was easy to travel around during the weekends, and where the weather was good.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was an unforgettable and amazing experience! I can highly recommend going on exchange in Australia - it has everything: good weather, wonderful nature and beaches, nice people and culture etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. UQ's website was very helpful, and I could easily find information about my courses and the academic calendar was very helpful to get an overview of the semester and the deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a lot of information from the councelors at UQ. The first day in the orientation week, we went to an oriention particurly made for exchange students, which was really helpful! Here we got useful information about enrolment of courses, deadlines etc. During the orientation week we also attended several useful seminars about safety in Australia, tour on Campus etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at Student One in the CBD area. It was easy to get a spot (if you apply a couple of months before going to Australia), but it was very expensive! But worth the money. It was nice living off campus, because UQ is located in the suburb St Lucia, which is around 5 km outside the CBD, and most of the UQ club events and the nice restaurants and cafes were in the CBD area, Fortitude Valley or West End.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Normally it is recommended to find housing after you arrive in Brisbane. However, it seems like COVID has changed that, and now it is very hard to find housing after arrival. Therefore: make sure to find housing before you go Brisbane. Mostly, the exchange students lived in share houses (for example in West end) or at the student accommandations such as Student One or Iglu.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The UQ website was easy to navigate in. I used the website to register and enrol my courses, find courses etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to use the website or sent an e-mail to UQ.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. I enrolled the courses before I came to Brisbane, and after arrival I had three weeks to change my courses, which was really nice. For example I switched one course after attending the first class.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to change your course after the semester has started - therefore, don't stress, if you don't like a course. You can easily change it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was not that high, but the workload at UQ could be very high. We spent a lot of time making assignments during the semester, because in every course the overall grade was depended on every assignment.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As previously described the overall academic level was not that high compared to UCPH. But it also depended on the course. I took some courses in indigenous politics and international relations in Asia Pacific, which was areas/regions I didn't knew much about before going to Australia.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very different compared to UCPH. At UQ the grade was depended on the attendence and the assigments during the semester, which is different from UCPH, where I normally have one exam in the end of the semester, that counts for the overall grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Indigenous Policy and Politics, International Relations in Asia-Pacific, Global Governance, Ethics and Human Rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can highly recommend taking a course in indigenous politics! It was very interesting learning about politics, society and culture in regard to the indigenous people of Australia.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying alcohol was very expensive - especially beers. But eating take away or eating at restaurants was not as expensive as I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UQ have so many clubs! Clubs for everything basically - sports clubs, clubs for different nationalities, clubs for different hobbies. They even have a club for Harry Potter fans. And it was easy just to sign up for the clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As previously described: UQ have so many clubs and there are a lot of opportunities when it comes to sports, social events etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined QUEST (club for exchange students) and the surf club, which I would highly recommend joining! The clubs arranged several events during the semester - for example trips to Byron Bay, Noosa and other amazing places in Australia, and it was very easy to get international friends in those clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just explore as much as Australia as possible :-) Go to Byron Bay, Sydney, Blue Mountains, Melbourne, Noosa, Sunshine Coast, Whitsundays, Cairns, Fraser Island, Uluru etc - there are lots of amazing nature, beaches, authentic surfer towns etc. to explore!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy - the Australian people are so nice and kind! And they have a very relaxed and informal tone and atmosphere.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't socialize much with locals. I mostly got friends from Europe and the US.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. The Australian culture is so relaxed and informal - it is easy to navigate in the differences between the australian and danish culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The calm and relaxed culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Explore Australia! Brisbane is well located in Australia - it is close to so many nice places.
2. Join the clubs at UQ! 
3. Remember to bring factor 50 sunscreen :-)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having the most amazing experiences in the most amazing country and getting new international friendships!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't experience many challenges.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
